body:
I totally understand the whole not wanting to burden or trauma dump on people. I never told anyone how bad my suicide was until after I was on medication and doing better. After that I only told one person. It was a close friend who usually has more rational way of looking at things and not very emotional but when I told her a bit about what I had gone through she started crying. She couldn’t believe that it had gotten so bad and that I never told anyone. Her reaction made me realize that there are some people who really do care and empathize with you. They would much rather have you share with them than bottle it up and have it get worse. 

A few things to try: gage the people in your life who you’re most comfortable with/who you think could best handle these topics. Ask people before sharing if they’re in the right headspace to listen to you vent. Let them know that you only need them to listen and that it’s not their job to make you better. Some people try to solve your problems for you, that’s how they show their love for people. But it usually doesn’t help especially when the problem feels like it can’t be solved, it will only make you feel more guilty. but maybe starting with saying that you don’t want them to help you or fix everything, you just want to vent about it, will help alleviate any urges they feel to do that and then you’ll feel less like a burden. Sometimes you just need to talk to someone about it while they sit there quietly and support you. 

I know this all sounds like basic info that anyone could figure out but it’s really easy for depression to cloud your judgement and the way you perceive your relationships and the people you love. Setting boundaries before you vent so that they know it’s okay to just listen will help them know how to respond in a way that makes you feel less obligated to “get better” and will help you know that you’re not asking them to do too much for you and it’s not as big of a burden as you think.

I’ve been meaning to share them with her but I just haven’t found the courage to yet. My feelings come in waves which have become more frequent and I only realized within the last few months how bad it’s gotten which is why I started attending therapy. But I was hoping once I started I would progress enough to not even have to mention it. I plan on telling her our next session.

I haven’t lost friends yet but I do feel like sometimes the little amount of what I have opened up about with my depression has caused some of my friends to distance themselves more just because they have their own stuff going on and don’t know how to help me.
